learningObjective: See how an input can cross a decision boundary while remaining inside the perturbation set allowed by a stated threat model.
mediumRationale: A deterministic SVG is the smallest useful medium for placing a clean point, a signed-gradient step, a decision boundary, and an L-infinity square in one checkable coordinate system. Mermaid expresses relationships but not continuous geometry; semantic HTML would turn spatial containment into a list; interaction would add controls without changing this fixed inference; reusing a paper figure would add licensing and empirical-context risk; mixed media is unnecessary; and no visual would leave the key distinction between ordinary accuracy and worst-case accuracy abstract.

pages.insight: The neighboring backpropagation slide explains how input gradients are assembled through the chain rule, but it does not discuss attacks or bounded input changes.
The loss-optimization slide presents a two-dimensional loss slice and gradient descent as following a local direction; this supports gradient intuition but operates in weight space.
The optimizer slide compares SGD, momentum, and adaptive updates in parameter space and adds no adversarial-input threat set.
The RAdam slide discusses optimizer variance and poor optima, not adversarial examples or worst-case input perturbations.

The SAM slide evaluates loss after a bounded adversarial perturbation to model weights. It is adjacent worst-case-neighborhood intuition, but its parameter-space geometry must not be presented as an input-space attack.
The following optimization divider contains no additional mechanism or adversarial-input figure.

deckReview.notes: All 214 pages of Basic_ML_CS_concepts were searched directly for adversarial, robust, threat-model, FGSM, projected-gradient, and worst-case language, then pages 44 through 49 were inspected in sequence. Page 48 is the only nearby adversarial-optimization usage and concerns SAM weight perturbations, not input attacks. Other keyword matches concern GANs, random-forest robustness, or generic algorithmic worst cases. No slide supplies the article's needed input-space threat-set geometry.

sourceReview.notes: The figure is an original schematic, not a reproduction of either paper or an empirical result. Its coordinates are disclosed in the SVG description and carry only the general mathematical claim that a bounded set may intersect another decision region. Public arXiv access was explicitly not treated as figure-reuse permission.

agentReview.summary: Reviewed the complete article, the full 214-page deck keyword sweep with neighboring pages 44-49, and the two primary attack papers. Selected one compact input-space schematic because the hardest prose-only model is that correctness at x says nothing about every allowed neighbor around x.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a title and a complete geometric description with coordinates. A circle versus diamond, solid arrow, dashed square and boundary, direct class labels, inequality text, and the caption preserve the full inference without color. Its 360-unit viewBox fits a 390 CSS-pixel viewport without a forced minimum width; shared figure variables provide dark-mode contrast and explicit print colors.
